Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot blunt the opponent's physical attackers, Scizor and Garchomp. Garchomp adds fast Mega pressure, and Gholdengo's special power covers Rotom-Wash and Ninetales-Alola.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Looking at team preview against their garchomp, rotomwash, scizor, incineroar, gholdengo, and ninetales-alola, I'm weighing my options: incineroar for intimidate/fake out/parting shot, garchomp with mega potential, gholdengo as a special attacker, plus kingambit, sinistcha, and archaludon. Scizor is vulnerable to incineroar's flare blitz, while their garchomp and ninetales-alola both threaten mine with ice coverage, so I need to think carefully about matchups there.

I'm settling on incineroar, garchomp, and gholdengo as a solid core — intimidate pressures their physical attackers like garchomp and scizor, garchomp brings speed and power, and gholdengo's steel/ghost typing gives good coverage against rotomwash and ninetales-alola while hitting hard offensively.

decisions.thought: 95% MOVE: earthquake, 4% SWITCH: rotomwash, 1% MOVE: stoneedge

Opposing Garchomp is faster than Incineroar, so it will act first and could hit hard, especially if it mega evolves. Fake Out is a guaranteed flinch on turn one that stops its first attack and chips it for 40 BP, which is the best opening here.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: The opponent's Garchomp likely holds Mega Stone and outspeeds Incineroar, so leading with Fake Out makes sense to drop its attack via Intimidate and deny its first move.

decisions.thought: 78% MOVE: earthquake, 17% SWITCH: rotomwash, 3% SWITCH: gholdengo

Opposing Garchomp is already at -1 Attack and is a physical threat, and Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon. Partingshot drops its Attack again and pivots Incineroar out, so Gholdengo can come in against a weakened Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type effectiveness for Flare Blitz against the Dragon/Ground Garchomp, which is sitting at 84% HP with Intimidate's -1 Attack drop already applied, and weighing whether its unrevealed item could be Garchompite for a Mega.

Switching Incineroar out via Parting Shot would further drop Garchomp's Attack while pivoting into Gholdengo, whose Thunderbolt is actually useless here since Garchomp is immune to Electric as a Ground type, though Shadow Ball and Make It Rain stay neutral options with Gholdengo's strong 203 Special Attack. I'm also weighing whether bringing in my own Garchomp from the bench might be the better play.

p is mostly physical, so that -2 cuts its damage significantly, and Gholdengo can then come in safely with Shadow Ball or Make It Rain while keeping Incineroar's HP intact. Flare Blitz feels too weak here, so I'll go with Partingshot.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is at 87 HP and would take heavy damage from Earthquake, which is super effective on it. Gholdengo would take 2x from Ground, so it's the worse switch. Garchomp resists nothing relevant but takes neutral damage from Earthquake, and the opposing Garchomp's Attack is already at -2.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 87/202 after that Earthquake, and Garchomp's attack is now lowered twice from Intimidate and Parting Shot. I'm weighing whether to switch to Garchomp or Gholdengo given the opponent's weakened attack stat.

Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost, so it's actually double weak to Ground - Earthquake would hit it hard even with the opponent's lowered attack. My own Garchomp is Dragon/Ground so Earthquake wouldn't be super effective against it, and comparing speed tiers, mine looks faster than theirs.

Switching in my Garchomp seems like the stronger play since it resists the Earthquake threat and can fire back with Earthquake or Outrage of its own, while Gholdengo would take a huge hit from Ground. I'll go with switching to Garchomp here.

Their Garchomp is at 84% HP (about 155 HP) and has -2 Attack. Outrage is super effective against a Dragon type, and our Garchomp's 182 Attack should KO it outright without spending Mega Evolution. Keep Mega in reserve.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the matchup between our Garchomp and the opponent's debuffed Garchomp—since both are Dragon/Ground, their Earthquake isn't super effective against ours, and their stat drops further reduce the threat.

I'm also comparing speed tiers: our non-Mega Garchomp sits at 169, while Mega Garchomp would shift the stat spread toward higher Attack and Defense, though I'm uncertain how Speed and ability (Sand Force vs Rough Skin) factor in if we mega evolve here.

Weighing Outrage against Earthquake, since Dragon-type Outrage hits the opposing Garchomp for 2x super effective damage with their Attack dropped by -2, I'm estimating whether non-Mega Outrage alone is enough to knock out their ~155 remaining HP, rather than needing to commit the mega evolution this turn.

Running the numbers, Outrage easily clears their remaining HP even without mega, so I don't need to burn the mega slot now. Speed-wise we're likely faster given the base stat similarities, so I'll just go with non-mega Outrage for the clean KO.

Mega evolving isn't necessary for the KO but could be useful long-term since it boosts Attack to 170 and Rotom-Wash's Levitate means Ground moves won't matter against it anyway—still, since regular Earthquake should already secure the Gholdengo kill, I don't see a strong reason to burn the Mega slot now.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:

Rotom-Wash is at 40% and Incineroar's Flare Blitz is a strong STAB hit, even with Water resisting Fire. Protect only delays and Parting Shot gives up the attacker while Incineroar is low. Flare Blitz is the best damage option now.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar is at 87/202 HP while Rotom-Wash sits at 40%. Flare Blitz is Fire-type, and since Rotom-Wash is Electric/Water, Water resists Fire for a 0.5x modifier overall, so this hit won't be as strong as I'd like despite the 120 base power.

Rolling through the damage math roughly, with Incineroar's attack and Rotom's defense scaled for level 50, Flare Blitz likely lands somewhere in the 50ish range after STAB and the resistance, which probably isn't enough to KO Rotom-Wash outright given its uncertain HP total. I'm weighing whether Parting Shot might be the safer play here to weaken and pivot out, especially since Gholdengo is still on the field at 46% and could punish Incineroar with Make It Rain if it stays in.

Given Rotom-Wash's bulk and the recoil risk from Flare Blitz, Parting Shot could set up a safer switch, but without knowing our reserve's HP it's a gamble either way -- I'll commit to Flare Blitz to keep pressure on since it's still our strongest damage option here.
